subject: math
cluster: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population
intro: A population is the whole group you want to learn about. A sample is the smaller part of that group you actually examine. A sample is random when every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen. Each problem below asks you to name the population, name the sample, or decide whether a sampling method is random.

items.prompt: A principal wants to know the favorite lunch of all $850$ students at a school. She surveys $50$ of the students. Identify the population.
items.answer: The population is all $850$ students at the school.

steps: The population is the whole group you want to learn about.
The principal wants to know about all $850$ students, so that whole group is the population.
The population is all $850$ students at the school.

items.prompt: A principal wants to know the favorite lunch of all $850$ students at a school. She surveys $50$ of the students. Identify the sample.
items.answer: The sample is the $50$ students who were surveyed.

steps: The sample is the part of the population that is actually examined.
Only $50$ students were surveyed, so those $50$ students are the sample.
The sample is the $50$ surveyed students.

items.prompt: A city official wants to know how all $12{,}000$ residents of a town feel about a new park. She asks $200$ residents. Identify the population and the sample.
items.answer: Population: all $12{,}000$ residents of the town. Sample: the $200$ residents who were asked.

steps: The population is the whole group of interest, which is all $12{,}000$ residents.
The sample is the subset actually examined, which is the $200$ residents who were asked.
Population: all $12{,}000$ residents. Sample: the $200$ residents asked.

items.prompt: A factory makes $5{,}000$ light bulbs in a day. A quality inspector tests $80$ of them. Identify the population.
items.answer: The population is all $5{,}000$ light bulbs made that day.

steps: The population is the whole group being studied.
The inspector wants to know about all $5{,}000$ bulbs, so they form the population.
The population is all $5{,}000$ light bulbs.

items.prompt: A factory makes $5{,}000$ light bulbs in a day. A quality inspector tests $80$ of them. Identify the sample.
items.answer: The sample is the $80$ light bulbs that were tested.

steps: The sample is the part of the population that is actually examined.
Only $80$ bulbs were tested, so those $80$ bulbs are the sample.
The sample is the $80$ tested light bulbs.

items.prompt: A teacher writes every student's name on an equal-sized slip of paper, mixes the slips in a bag, and draws $5$ names without looking. Is this a random sample? Answer yes or no.
items.answer: Yes. It is a random sample because every student has an equal chance of being chosen.

steps: A sample is random when every member of the population has an equal chance of being selected.
Each name is on an equal-sized slip, the slips are mixed, and they are drawn without looking, so every student is equally likely to be picked.
Yes, this is a random sample.

items.prompt: A reporter interviews the first $20$ people who walk out of a movie theater. Is choosing the first $20$ people a random sample? Answer yes or no.
items.answer: No. It is not a random sample because not every moviegoer had an equal chance of being chosen.

steps: A random sample gives every member of the population an equal chance of being selected.
Only the people who happened to leave first were chosen, so people who left later had no chance of being picked.
No, this is not a random sample.

items.prompt: Each student in a school is given a number, and a computer picks $30$ numbers completely at random. Is this a random sample? Answer yes or no.
items.answer: Yes. It is a random sample because every student has an equal chance of being selected.

steps: A random sample means every member of the population is equally likely to be chosen.
The computer picks numbers completely at random, so each numbered student has the same chance of being selected.
Yes, this is a random sample.

items.prompt: A coach asks only the members of the basketball team what they think of the new gym rules. Is this a random sample of all students? Answer yes or no.
items.answer: No. It is not a random sample because only basketball players could be chosen, not every student.

steps: A random sample of all students would give every student an equal chance of being selected.
Only basketball team members were asked, so students who are not on the team had no chance of being chosen.
No, this is not a random sample.

items.prompt: A grocery store wants to know what all of its shoppers think of its prices. It surveys $100$ shoppers. What is the population in this situation?
items.answer: The population is all of the store's shoppers.

steps: The population is the whole group the store wants to learn about.
The store wants to know about all of its shoppers, so they are the population.
The population is all of the store's shoppers.

items.prompt: A grocery store wants to know what all of its shoppers think of its prices. It surveys $100$ shoppers. What is the sample in this situation?
items.answer: The sample is the $100$ shoppers who were surveyed.

steps: The sample is the subset of the population that is actually examined.
Only $100$ shoppers were surveyed, so those $100$ shoppers are the sample.
The sample is the $100$ surveyed shoppers.

items.prompt: A librarian spins a fair spinner to pick which shelves to check and ends up choosing books so that every book has an equal chance of being selected. Is this method random or not random?
items.answer: Random. Every book has an equal chance of being selected.

steps: A method is random when every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.
The problem states every book has an equal chance of being selected, so the method is random.
The method is random.

items.prompt: A radio station asks listeners to call in and share their opinion. Only listeners who choose to call are counted. Is this a random sample? Answer yes or no.
items.answer: No. It is not a random sample because only listeners who choose to call are included.

steps: A random sample gives every member of the population an equal chance of being selected.
Only listeners who decide to call are counted, so listeners who do not call have no chance of being included.
No, this is not a random sample.

items.prompt: A scientist wants to study all the fish in a large lake. She catches $60$ fish to examine. Identify the population.
items.answer: The population is all the fish in the lake.

steps: The population is the whole group being studied.
The scientist wants to learn about all the fish in the lake, so they are the population.
The population is all the fish in the lake.

items.prompt: A scientist wants to study all the fish in a large lake. She catches $60$ fish to examine. Identify the sample.
items.answer: The sample is the $60$ fish that were caught and examined.

steps: The sample is the part of the population that is actually examined.
Only $60$ fish were caught and examined, so those $60$ fish are the sample.
The sample is the $60$ caught fish.
